title: The voice that is not allowed to know anything
angle: Live. Four grounded tools are the agent's whole vocabulary, and Deepgram calls our API server-to-server so the manual never enters the tab.
endline: Don't trust the voice. Trust the page.

marks.do: The lift. 20% of his week. He refuses AI, and he is right to.
The one rule, verbatim. "Not a style guide — a permission set."
Four functions, one book. The architecture.
LIVE. Six utterances. Interrupt it. Ask it about a Ducati.
Where the milliseconds go. Volunteer the slow one.
What of Deepgram, and why — including what we could not prove.

slides.text: Both hands on the bike, oil on the gloves, a phone on the bench he will not touch.
slides.sub: *20%* of his working time goes to manuals — *EUR 36–48k* of billable time a year. He will not use AI: 95% correct is not good enough when he is liable for the 5%, and one question cost him about *$4*. This is the case voice was invented for, and the case where a voice assistant that improvises is at its most dangerous — *because there is no page on screen to catch it.*
notes: A real person with a real number attached to the problem, and a real reason he has refused every product in this category so far.
"A wrong torque figure does not produce a wrong paragraph. It produces a wheel that comes off."
Say ~he says~. Thirty seconds, then move to the rule.

slides.text: You do not know anything about this motorcycle. Everything you think you remember about a KTM, a BMW or any other bike is wrong here and may not be spoken. Call a function FIRST, every single time, before the first word of every answer.
slides.cite: api/app/voice.py — the prompt's one rule, verbatim
notes: "This is the system prompt. *It is not a style guide, it is a permission set.*"

And for numbers specifically: *a torque, a capacity, a pressure, a clearance, a gap, an interval, a fuse rating or a part number may only leave your mouth if a function result you have already received printed it, word for word.*
A voice answer has no citation — there is no hyperlink in a sound wave. So the grounding cannot be a footnote you add afterwards. It has to be the only thing the agent is able to do.
*Don't trust the voice. Trust the page.* The voice is a pointer, not an authority.

slides.title: Four functions, one book
slides.caption: One socket — listen, think, speak. The agent's whole vocabulary is our four grounded tools, and the manual's text never enters the tab.
notes: "Deepgram calls our API. The manual never enters the browser. The manual id is in the URL, not in the model's arguments." Then stop reading the diagram.
Because the functions carry an `endpoint`, the tool calls are server-to-server. The browser cannot forge a tool result, and the agent physically cannot answer from a book it was not handed.

We found out the hard way the page cannot be left to the model: 7 spoken turns, 6 pages named out loud, *0 show_page calls* — including on "show me the brake fluid procedure". So the reader no longer waits for the model to decide.

The key: a Workers WebSocket defaults to blob, and a Blob handed back to send() goes out as the literal text [object Blob] — which silently turns every PCM frame into UNPARSABLE_CLIENT_MESSAGE while the JSON keeps flowing perfectly. Good war story if they lean in.

A judge who watches you volunteer your own slowest path believes the rest of your numbers.

Numbers are spoken, not printed: the prompt bans every screen-only token. Over 8 live turns every *figure* came out spelled. Two turns leaked a printed *grade* through — SAE 15W/50 and DOT 4 — and aura-2 reads those as letters. *Do not claim 8/8; claim what it is.*

slides.title: What of Deepgram, and why
head: why
rows: *Voice Agent API*, not STT + LLM + TTS stitched

One socket carries mic up, voice down and the JSON events interleaved — so the turn boundary, the barge-in signal and the function call are decided next to the audio. And the tool calls are *server-side*, which is what makes the grounding airtight.

End of turn is detected inside the model, not by a silence timer. Eager EOT starts the LLM before the sentence ends and throws the speculative turn away on TurnResumed. *1.35 s to first audio against nova-3's 1.97 s.*
A workshop answer is often wrong-question-shaped. Scheduled audio dies on the next render quantum, *<3 ms*.

cells: Accepted live with zero errors. *We could not measure a win:* 11.4% vs 13.6% WER at 3 dB, 14.1% vs 13.3% at 0 dB. That is noise, not a result. It ships because it is the documented lever, it costs nothing, and it protects the proper nouns.

slides.note: The claim we are entitled to make is *"built and wired"*, not *"X% better"*. A real number needs real mechanics in a real shop — and that is the first thing we would spend a Deepgram credit on.
notes: "One socket instead of three. Endpointing inside the model. And a feature we shipped and could not prove — here is the data."
*A judge who hears you refuse an easy number will believe the ones you do give.* This is the best slide in the deck for exactly that reason.

think.provider.type is open_ai: Deepgram drives think through /v1/chat/completions, which rejects reasoning_effort the moment function tools are attached — so reasoning models close the socket with FAILED_TO_THINK. This is not "Deepgram instead of OpenAI", it is Deepgram's transport and turn-taking around OpenAI's reasoning.
